title: Finiteness over an integral map of adequate moduli spaces
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal U,\mathcal V$ be algebraic stacks of finite type over $k$ (finite type tested on smooth scheme charts), and let $p:\mathcal U\to P$ and $q:\mathcal V\to Q$ be adequate moduli spaces [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. Let $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ and $g:P\to Q$ be $k$-morphisms with a specified 2-isomorphism $qf\simeq gp$. Assume that $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces, quasi-finite and separated, that $g$ is integral, and that $|f|$ sends every closed point of $|\mathcal U|$ to a closed point of $|\mathcal V|$. Then $f$ is finite. Here representable means that every pullback by a scheme is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]; quasi-finite and separated mean finite type with finite geometric fibres and closed relative diagonal on these algebraic-space tests. Finite type uses [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Finite and integral for representable maps mean that every scheme base change is a scheme with the respective property [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The point space of a stack is the set of field-valued objects up to isomorphism after common field extension, with the topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas; a closed point means a closed singleton in this topology. As in the source's Section 2 conventions, assume also that the diagonals of $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$ are quasi-compact and separated (tested after scheme charts, with quasi-compactness as in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]).

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1, hypotheses (a)--(c), printed p.39. Primary PDF read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398v3; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-quasifinite-relative-normalization] to $f$. Its representability, quasi-finiteness, separatedness and diagonal assumptions are exactly those stated here. Obtain $f=hj$ with $j:\mathcal U\hookrightarrow\mathcal N=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{\mathcal V}\mathcal A$ open and $h$ integral, where $\mathcal A\subseteq f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$ is the integral-closure algebra. Retain this actual algebra: replacing it by an arbitrary finite Zariski-main envelope would not justify the section comparison below.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1, printed p.39; integral-relative-normalization expansion of the factorization and Lemma 5.2.11 step.

proof.text: The section formula of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] and the specified $qf\simeq gp$ identify $(qf)_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}=g_*p_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}=g_*\mathcal O_P$, using the structure-sheaf isomorphism of [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. Thus $q_*\mathcal A$ is a subalgebra of $g_*\mathcal O_P$. Conversely take an affine etale test $T=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Q$. Since $g$ is integral, $P_T=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with every $b\in B$ satisfying a monic polynomial over $R$. The corresponding section on $\mathcal U_T$ satisfies the same polynomial after restriction to each smooth affine chart $S\to\mathcal V_T$. Its coefficients now lie in $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$, so the section belongs to the integral-closure algebra $\mathcal A|_S$ of step 1. These restrictions agree because they are restrictions of the same section; hence they glue as a section of $\mathcal A$ on $\mathcal V_T$. Therefore $q_*\mathcal A=g_*\mathcal O_P$ on every affine etale test, with the same restriction maps.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1, printed p.39; integral-relative-normalization expansion of the factorization and Lemma 5.2.11 step.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adequate-relative-spectrum] to $q$ and $\mathcal A$. The resulting adequate moduli space is $\bar p:\mathcal N\to\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Q(q_*\mathcal A)$. Step 2 identifies its target with $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Q(g_*\mathcal O_P)=P$: on each affine etale $T\to Q$ this is the identity $\operatorname{Spec}B=P_T$, since $g$ is integral and hence affine on scheme tests. The evaluation maps give $\bar p j\simeq p$; on every such test their maps of functions both send $b$ to its pullback on $\mathcal U_T$. Thus the original moduli morphism and the one on the normalization have the same target, without assuming arbitrary base change preserves adequate moduli spaces.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1, printed p.39; integral-relative-normalization expansion of the factorization and Lemma 5.2.11 step.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-integral-stack-closed-point-topology], $h$ is closed and every point over a closed point of $\mathcal V$ is closed in $\mathcal N$. If $C\subseteq|\mathcal N|$ is nonempty closed, then $h(C)$ is nonempty closed in $|\mathcal V|$. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-stack-closed-specialization] it contains a closed point $v$; any $x\in C$ over $v$ is closed in $\mathcal N$. Hence every nonempty closed subset of $|\mathcal N|$ has a closed point, although $\mathcal N$ was not assumed Noetherian. Moreover, if $u$ is closed in $\mathcal U$, then $f(u)$ is closed by the hypothesis on $f$, and $h(j(u))=f(u)$ shows that $j(u)$ is closed in $\mathcal N$.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1, printed p.39; integral-relative-normalization expansion of the factorization and Lemma 5.2.11 step.

proof.text: If the complement of the open $j(\mathcal U)$ is nonempty, step 4 supplies a point $x$ in that complement closed in $\mathcal N$. By [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-topological-images] applied to $\bar p$, its image $y=\bar p(x)$ is closed: the singleton $\{x\}$ is a reduced closed substack by [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets], and adequate moduli morphisms have closed images. The same adequate-moduli theorem applied to $p$ makes $p^{-1}(y)$ nonempty; it is closed by continuity. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-stack-closed-specialization] choose a point $u$ of this fibre closed in $\mathcal U$. Then $j(u)$ is closed in $\mathcal N$ by step 4. Apply the intersection-of-closed-images clause to the reduced singleton substacks $\{x\}$ and $\{j(u)\}$ of $\mathcal N$. Both images are $\{y\}$, so their intersection has nonempty image. Their underlying singleton subsets must intersect, giving $x=j(u)$, a contradiction.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1, printed p.39; integral-relative-normalization expansion of the factorization and Lemma 5.2.11 step.

proof.text: Therefore $j$ is a surjective open immersion, hence an isomorphism: on each scheme test its open subscheme has the whole underlying space and thus is the entire scheme. Consequently $f$ is integral, since it is identified with $h$ from step 1. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal V$, integrality makes $\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal V}T$ a scheme integral over $T$; the finite-type assumption in quasi-finiteness makes this map locally of finite type. Apply [pqf-lem-integral-lft-finite] to this scheme morphism. Every such test is finite, which is exactly the stated finiteness of $f$.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1, printed p.39; integral-relative-normalization expansion of the factorization and Lemma 5.2.11 step.
